mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS has declined over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.0% in a 3-month window, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between rising federal funds rate and rising unemployment rate (indicating a tightening monetary policy coinciding with labor market weakness) creates a negative feedback loop that depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The negative return prediction fails when the interaction term (FEDFUNDS * UNRATE) is positive and SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC for the interaction model is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, rising housing starts (HOUST) signal strong consumer demand and economic momentum, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods during late-cycle expansion when HOUST is rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over the past 3 months reflects robust consumer demand and economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST has increased over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100.0 in a 3-month window, it indicates a contraction in manufacturing output that reduces corporate profits and causes negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO is below 100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals reduced liquidity and higher discount rates, which depress equity valuations and lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS is rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past 3 months indicates a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS has increased over the past 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
